gloss: easily bored; fickle; having a short attention span

definitions.gloss: easily bored; fickle; quick to lose interest
definitions.explanation: Describes a personality trait of getting bored or losing interest quickly. Used to characterize someone who starts things enthusiastically but soon tires of them.

examples.japanese: {飽|あ}きっぽい{性格|せいかく}を{直|なお}したい。
examples.english: I want to fix my fickle personality.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{飽|あ}きっぽいから、{長|なが}い{映画|えいが}は{向|む}かない。
examples.english: Children get bored easily, so long movies aren't suited for them.

notes:
Describes someone who loses interest in things quickly — the kind of person who picks up hobbies but drops them soon after. It carries a mildly negative nuance, suggesting a lack of perseverance.

FORMS:
{飽|あ}きる (to get tired of) + っぽい (tendency suffix). The っぽい suffix indicates a habitual tendency or characteristic.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飽|あ}きっぽい{性格|せいかく}: fickle personality
- {飽|あ}きっぽい{人|ひと}: someone who gets bored easily
- {飽|あ}きっぽくて{続|つづ}かない: too fickle to stick with something

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {三日坊主|みっかぼうず}: someone who can't stick with anything (literally "three-day monk") — emphasizes inability to continue, while {飽|あ}きっぽい focuses on the tendency to lose interest
- {気|き}まぐれ: whimsical, capricious — broader meaning covering unpredictable behavior, not just boredom

cross_references.label: someone who can't stick with anything
